sourceRules.notes: Application-state settings semantics remain implemented in the native SettingsModel; there is no Rust settings owner in R08.
Color-scheme model, JSON, inheritance and mutation semantics remain native SettingsModel responsibilities with no Rust owner.
Settings command-model semantics remain native C++/WinRT product logic; they are not UI-only and have not transferred to Rust.
Settings deserialization and layering semantics remain in native SettingsModel with no Rust equivalent.
Key-binding model and action-binding semantics remain native SettingsModel responsibilities; terminal-input Rust does not own this product settings contract.
Media-resource settings semantics remain in the native SettingsModel. Platform-facing resource resolution is not a reason to claim a Rust equivalent.
New-tab menu settings-model semantics remain native product logic; no Rust settings owner exists.
Profile model semantics remain native SettingsModel behavior with no Rust owner.
Settings serialization and round-trip semantics remain native SettingsModel behavior with no Rust equivalent.
Terminal-settings composition and projection remain native SettingsModel behavior; no Rust settings crate owns these contracts.
Theme model semantics remain native SettingsModel behavior; XAML consumption does not make the model itself UI-managed.
FZF source methods default to Missing unless H09 supplies an individual Exact Rust witness. The Microsoft-ignored multi-code-point full-fold contract intentionally remains Missing.
TerminalApp JSON utility semantics remain native C++ product logic with no Rust equivalent.
Terminal application command-line semantics remain native C++ product logic; terminal-host argument parsing is a different contract and is not credited here.
Filtered command/product action semantics remain native TerminalApp logic with no Rust owner.
TerminalApp settings integration remains native product logic; it is not merely XAML orchestration and has not transferred to Rust.

These tests deliberately activate UAP/XAML, construct XAML controls, dispatch work to the UI thread and exercise TerminalPage/tab UI orchestration. This responsibility stays on the XAML/managed product side rather than being shadow-migrated into Rust.

The suite directly constructs C++/WinRT ControlCore through COM apartments, projected settings/connection interfaces and renderer/control platform boundaries. Lower-level terminal semantics already have their own Rust-suite evidence and are not double-counted here.

The suite directly constructs C++/WinRT ControlInteractivity, uses COM apartments and Windows pointer/mouse/control event surfaces. Portable terminal selection/input contracts remain tracked in their owning Rust stages rather than replacing this boundary suite.
